newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Small-caps, electronics to lift Singapore stocks.
newsitem.headline: Small-caps, electronics to lift Singapore stocks.

text.p: Interest in small-capitalised stocks, notably selective electronic counters, was seen providing further lift to Singapore's stock market on Friday, dealers said.

"Blue chips are unlikely to move so much as small-cap, electronics stocks. People seem more willing to put their money in these as they could provide faster returns and are more affordable," said a local dealer.
Despite the improvement in sentiment on Thursday, chartists said the key Straits Times Industrials (STI) index was looking ill, and could sink below 1,900.
Concerns over unstable regional currencies continued to weigh on the market.
On Thursday, the index ended 2.65 points higher at 1,920.54, halting six consecutive sessions of losses.
